Describe how you would investigate the issue step by step, including: How you would collect evidence How you would isolate likely causes How you would communicate progress to stakeholders How you would prevent the issue from recurring

Explain how you would design: Heartbeat and stale-record handling Multiple devices for one user Concurrent state updates Cache and persistent storage Recovery when one presence-service instance fails

Describe a time when you had to work with product managers, QA engineers, infrastructure engineers, or frontend engineers to deliver a technical feature. How did you handle: Conflicting priorities Unclear requirements Technical disagreements Final delivery coordination

Design a backend API for scheduling online meetings. It must support creation, updates, cancellation, recurrence, and participants in different time zones. Explain: Resources and endpoints Validation and authorization Idempotent client requests Conflicting updates Backward-compatible API evolution

Design a reliable delivery service covering: Event schema and versioning Request signing Retries and backoff Duplicate delivery and idempotency Ordering expectations Dead-letter handling and monitoring

A platform stores recording files in object storage while a backend service manages their metadata. Design the service, covering: Meeting, owner, and tenant linkage Processing status Search and indexing Access control Retention and deletion Missing or partially uploaded objects

A backend feature must generate a large report that takes several minutes. Design this asynchronously. Handing off work without blocking the request Notifying the user when ready Handling a job that fails partway Preventing duplicate concurrent generation

A production issue occurs shortly after a change you contributed to, but it is not yet clear whether your change caused the problem. What would you do? Describe how you would approach: Responsibility Investigation Communication Mitigation Follow-up improvements

A meeting platform sends invitations, reminders, and cancellation notices through email, push, and in-app channels. Design the notification backend, including: Templates and user preferences Scheduled delivery Large-list fan-out Deduplication Provider failures and rate limits Delivery monitoring

A meeting service integrates with several third-party calendar providers. Design an integration layer covering: Provider adapters OAuth token refresh Rate-limit and transient-error handling Mapping external events to internal meetings Webhook synchronization Safe handling of provider API changes

Session metadata must remain available if one cloud region fails. Design a cross-region approach. Discuss: Authoritative state Consistency requirements Conflict resolution Failover and stale reads Reconciliation after recovery How you would test the design

Meeting plans allow different maximum participant counts. Design a mechanism that remains correct when many users join concurrently. Explain: Atomic capacity checks Duplicate and retry handling Capacity release after disconnects Administrator overrides Consistency across service instances Monitoring and alerts

Design the backend state for a meeting waiting room. Participants wait while hosts admit or reject them, and clients may reconnect. Discuss: Queue and participant states Authorization Concurrent host actions Timeouts Client state updates Failure recovery and scaling

All participants in the same meeting must observe consistent behaviour even when they use different client versions or connect through different backend instances. Design a feature-flag approach covering tenant targeting, meeting-level consistency, configuration propagation, backward compatibility, audit history, rollback, and safe defaults.

A regulated customer requires an audit trail for meeting-administration actions. Design the backend, including: Actor, action, target, time, and result Tamper-evident storage Retention and archival Search and reporting Access control Personal-data minimization

A participant briefly loses connectivity and then rejoins a meeting. Design the backend recovery flow. Explain: Secure session identification Reconnect grace periods Idempotent rejoin Duplicate-connection handling Stale-state cleanup Replaying missed state changes

Your backend runs scheduled background jobs (cleanup, reporting, syncing) via a job scheduler. Design for reliability. Preventing concurrent duplicate runs Handling jobs that repeatedly fail Monitoring whether jobs keep pace Changing a schedule without missing or duplicating a run

A communication platform contains separate session, notification, and recording-metadata services. Design health monitoring for them, covering: Liveness and readiness Service-level indicators Metrics, logs, and tracing Dependency failures Alert thresholds Dashboards and alert-storm prevention

Discuss: Primary keys and foreign keys Timestamp storage Query patterns for searching logs Retention and archival strategy How you would optimize storage and query performance

How would you decide whether to use a relational database, a non-relational database, or both? Explain: Data structure requirements Consistency needs Query complexity Scalability expectations Long-term management and maintenance considerations

Cover: Backward compatibility Migration scripts Rollback planning Data validation Deployment sequencing How to avoid downtime or service disruption

Explain: Connection pool sizing Long-running queries Leaked connections Transaction duration Monitoring metrics Ways to optimize connection management

Participant join, leave, and meeting-status changes must reach downstream notification and analytics services. Design the event stream, covering: Schema versioning Partitioning and ordering Duplicate events Replay and retention Consumer lag and back-pressure Dead-letter handling

Only one participant should control content sharing at a time. Design the backend coordination state without discussing media transport. Explain: Acquiring and releasing control Concurrent requests Heartbeat and timeout rules Host override Disconnect cleanup State distribution and recovery

Your team is migrating a backend service from an on-premises data center to the cloud. Plan this migration. Sequencing what moves first vs. last Keeping the service available throughout Validating cloud behavior matches on-prem Rolling back if migration fails badly

Two backend services must stay in sync: one updates a record, the other must eventually reflect it. Design this synchronization. Sync vs. eventual consistency Resolving conflicting updates Recovering from downtime during an update Verifying the two haven't drifted apart

Include: Deployment steps Configuration details Common failure scenarios Monitoring dashboards Alert descriptions Rollback procedures Escalation paths

Explain how you would scale session and participant services using: Horizontal scaling and load balancing Stateless and stateful components Distributed storage and caching Failure recovery Capacity and reliability testing

Walk through the complete end-to-end call setup process and identify the role of: Q.931 H.225 H.245 H.235 SIP SDP At which stages would protocol translation be required, and how would you troubleshoot a failure where call signaling succeeds but media never establishes?

Specifically discuss: CPU consumption Network bandwidth utilization Transcoding requirements Media quality adaptation Conference scale limits Failure domains Then justify which architecture you would recommend and why.

Describe: The signaling sequence required to establish dual streams The media flows involved Common failure points How you would verify whether the issue is caused by endpoint capability negotiation, conference policy restrictions, or media-engine resource exhaustion.

Explain how you would tune: Jitter buffers RTP/RTCP behavior Codec parameters (H.264/H.265) Keyframe generation strategy Audio/video synchronization mechanisms Describe the trade-offs between latency, smoothness, and image quality.

Explain: HDMI routing Audio transport using XLR/RCA Control signaling Optical versus electrical transmission choices Failure risks introduced by each stage of the signal chain.

A customer reports: Echo during meetings Inconsistent microphone volume Excessive background noise Design the real-time audio processing chain and explain the ordering and interaction of: AEC ANS AGC Why does algorithm order matter, and what artifacts would you expect if AGC is applied before ANS or if AEC is incorrectly tuned?

Explain: ASR streaming pipeline LLM orchestration layer MCP/function-calling workflow TTS generation Media reinjection into the conference Latency budget allocation across each component Finally, identify the biggest technical bottleneck that would prevent the experience from feeling truly real-time.

In a WebRTC-based video conference, both RTP and RTCP packets are exchanged. Explain: What RTP is responsible for What RTCP is responsible for Why both protocols are required What problems would occur if RTCP packets were blocked while RTP continued to flow
